newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends up on exports, weather jitters.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends up on exports, weather jitters.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher, with nearbys boosted by spillover strength from CBOT wheat and new crop months seeing support from worries about cold weather next week, traders said.

"The fresh input today was an expansion of world export demand. Chicago reflected that and we followed their prices higher," a trader said. "At the same time, our back months drew strength from the blast of arctic air that's (expected) next week."
Forecasters said tempereatures will drop into the single digits (F) next week in the southern and central U.S. Plains.

Wheat opened higher after a bullish weekly export report and on news that India will need to import two million tonnes of wheat in the near-term. But traders said KCBT lagged CBOT wheat because of weak cash basis levels for HRW wheat.
KCBT wheat closed 1-3/4 to six cents per bushel higher, with Dec up 1-3/4 cents at $4.52. March gained 3-3/4 cents to settle at $4.05-1/2.

Traders said U.S. wheat markets were also encouraged after the EU granted 477,000 tonnes of free-market wheat at 17.47 Ecus per tonne -- a move that was seen by some as keeping European prices in line with U.S. values.

Volumes were active, and traders said Smoot Grain and CIS each bought at least 1.6 million March bushels. Term Commodities, Benson-Quinn and LFG all sold at least one million March. Term and LFG also sold 1.2 million July each.
